svg.aria-label: The road surface image as a dense-detection primitive. Left: six properties of the frame — thin elongated targets, low contrast and confounders, a fixed taxonomy tied to standards, a moving capture platform with heavy overlap, physical units that matter, and long-tailed classes and severities. Right: a ladder of six output layers from L0 capture geometry and geolocation, L1 image-level distress classification, L2 boxes per distress, L3 pixel masks and skeletons, L4 measurement of width, length, area and depth, to L5 severity, pavement condition index and maintenance decision.
svg.title: The road surface image: six properties, six output layers
svg.text: The road surface image: six frame properties, six output layers
Dashcam, survey vehicle, drone or 3D laser profiler. The answer an agency needs is a condition score per road section, not a box.

g.text: Cracks are 1–5 px wide and hundreds long: boxes are mostly road.
Joints, tar seals, shadows, oil, lane paint and wet patches.
ASTM D6433 / national manuals define type and severity.
4 · A moving camera with heavy overlap
The same pothole appears in 10–50 frames; count it once.
Width in mm, area in m², depth in cm: needs calibration.
Longitudinal cracks dominate; asphalt and camera vary by region.
PaveGPT, VLM street-view mapping, PCI regression (§8)
L4 · Measurement: width, length, area, depth
SCSegamba, CrackGeoFM, SAM3 decoders, instance masks (§4–5)
distress / no distress, satellite condition rating (§8)

svg.text: Blue: perception layers with public benchmarks. Orange: engineering layers where evaluation against field measurement is still rare.
